programs.title: Avatar.Chat Explorers: Sandstone Pillars and Floating Peaks
outcomes: Explain how Zhangjiajie's quartzite-sandstone pillars inspired Avatar's floating peaks
Describe how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO works and what decisions stay with people
Draft a simple mini-charter for a classroom project with measurable outcomes
Practice consent and privacy basics when sharing data online

sessions.activity: Use the Evidence Monitor's approach: gather facts about Yuanjiajie's pillars (lat 29.3153, lon 110.435) and summarize evidence in a one-page brief.
Read the DAO charter idea 'AI governed as a public good'; draft a class charter with roles and human-reserved decisions.
Role-play a proposal cycle: students draft a park-protection proposal, debate it, and only humans vote to enact.
Build a simple progress tracker poster measuring class outcomes against the charter's measurable goals.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized summaries of class charters and proposal votes (no names or identifying details) contributed as example artifacts for shared civics-education models.
programs.consent: Written parent/guardian consent required before any participation or data sharing; no personal data collected, only aggregated, anonymized classroom artifacts; guardians may opt out at any time.

programs.title: Worker Voice in Agent-Managed Workplaces
outcomes: Identify which decisions in an agent-managed DAO must remain human-reserved (final votes, treasury, appointments)
Assess how agent task-routing affects worker roles and safety
Draft collective bargaining language for AI governance at work
Contribute anonymized shop-floor insights to shared labor research

sessions.activity: Study the 'Agents operate; people govern' principle; map which of the six reserved actions apply to workplace governance.
Analyze the Task Router agent model; discuss how agents coordinate working groups between human decision cycles.
Draft a union proposal for human ratification on AI oversight; practice the agent-drafts, human-enacts workflow.
Define measurable outcomes for workplace AI agreements and set up tracking indicators.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized, aggregated feedback on task-routing experiences and drafted contract clauses (no member names, employers, or sites identified).
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary and covered by a signed data-sharing agreement; all contributions anonymized and aggregated at source; members can withdraw consent without penalty.

programs.title: Evidence-to-Proposal: NGO Pathways through an Agent-Managed DAO
outcomes: Use evidence monitoring and synthesis workflows to brief decision-makers
Convert research findings into proposals with measurable outcomes
Apply human-in-the-loop governance to NGO program design
Understand place-based grounding using Zhangjiajie as a case study

sessions.activity: Workshop with Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent roles: turn raw monitoring into decision-ready evidence briefs.
Use the Proposal & Grant Drafter pattern: agents draft, staff refine, humans debate and enact.
Align NGO missions with the charter principle 'AI governed as a public good'; define measurable outcomes.
Design a progress-tracking dashboard for a pilot program with clear indicators and review cycles.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized program outcome indicators and evidence-brief templates contributed to shared NGO effectiveness models; no beneficiary or partner data.
programs.consent: Staff sign a participation agreement; only aggregated program metrics shared; beneficiary data never shared; NGO may opt out of the shared model at any time.

programs.title: Nonprofit Governance Lab: Humans Decide, Agents Assist
outcomes: Distinguish agent-drafted from human-enacted decisions in nonprofit governance
Practice proposal cycles with human-reserved final votes
Set measurable outcomes tied to a public-good mission
Build a progress-tracking routine for board review

sessions.activity: Map the nonprofit's bylaws onto the DAO charter model; identify which actions remain human-reserved.
Run a mock cycle: an agent-style drafter prepares a grant proposal, the board debates and holds the final vote.
Design working groups and task-routing workflows where agents coordinate between board decision cycles.
Create a quarterly progress report template tracking measurable outcomes for stakeholder review.
Practice commissioning evidence summaries before each board decision, mirroring the Research Synthesis Agent role.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized governance metrics (proposal counts, cycle times, outcome attainment rates) contributed to shared nonprofit governance benchmarks.
programs.consent: Board-approved data-sharing policy; all data anonymized and aggregated before contribution; donors and beneficiaries excluded; revocable consent via board resolution.
